ZH supplementation of Holstein steers for 20 d prior harvest resulted in increased carcass quality, as defined by the USDA grading system, and increased carcass yield, as defined by CGBA grading system.
ZH supplementation of cattle results in increased carcass yield, but the magnitude of the increase is less than the increase in yield with additional days on feed.

carcasses from steers supplemented with Zilpaterol for 20 d and harvested at 534 DOFF had 8.7% more longissimus muscle area, 0.33 less USDA yield grade, 4.6% more JMGA longissimus muscle, 0.005 more JMGA subcutaneous fat, and 0.07 more USDA marbling than carcasses from control steers harvested at 534 days on feed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ZH treatment does not impact the CBGA or JMGA grading outcomes, but it does have a large impact on USDA grading outcomes.
ZH supplementation and increased DOF have the greatest impact on LM area and yield, which is important to the USDA, CBAG, and JMGA.
ZH-fed steers have a greater LM area, which is the primary determinant for the USDA YG and the JMGA estimated yield, and that increasing DOF results in greater LM area and subcutaneous fat thickness.
